claims.text: Severe plastic deformation can improve the strength-ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn relative to the unmodified alloy.
The proposed improvement will occur under dynamic loading across different temperatures and strain rates.
Cryo-rolling or high-pressure torsion will introduce a heterogeneous lattice strain field into Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The heterogeneous lattice strain field is caused by severe atomic lattice distortion.
A heterogeneous lattice strain field produces multiple dislocation-pinning sites and makes dislocation motion sluggish.
The heterogeneous lattice strain field forces dislocations to follow wavy trajectories.
The heterogeneous lattice strain field promotes multiple dislocation kinks and jogs.
The heterogeneous lattice strain field promotes bidirectional cross-slip.
The altered dislocation motion increases dislocation density and entanglement.
Increased dislocation density and entanglement produce forest strengthening.
The proposed dislocation mechanisms increase strain hardening and thereby enable strength-ductility synergy.
The intervention may increase yield strength relative to unmodified Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The intervention may increase ultimate tensile strength relative to unmodified Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The intervention may increase elongation to failure relative to unmodified Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The hypothesis is valid from 77 K to 900 K.
The hypothesis is valid from strain rates of 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^7 s^-1.
Micropillar compression and discrete dislocation dynamics simulations can be used to examine the effects of lattice strain on dislocation behavior and strength.
Failure to obtain a significant increase in both yield strength and strain hardening would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The design specifies micropillar compression, but ultimate tensile strength and tensile elongation to failure are listed as measurements; these tensile quantities are not directly obtained from a micropillar compression test.
